analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: the date bump, and the Nemotron Super inline-media body cap described as 8 MiB → 40 MiB with a new `media_too_large` error (head lines ~128-132, 542-544). The supplied evidence contains no source code changes, so no control is altered in this diff. It is documentation drift only.

Security relevance: if the code really raises `maximumEncodedBodyBytes` to 40 MiB, the ingress memory charge happens before JSON/base64/header inspection and media is charged before decode (base lines 82-83, 130-131). The doc says the shared-budget charge still returns a media-memory 503 when it cannot be held. This touches availability/memory-exhaustion considerations around the provider inference engine (TB-007, T-029) and the plaintext prompt/media handling inside the provider process (A-001, TB-003). The diff does not show the charge scaling or the transports. The statement that the cap 'holds every body the provider's transports deliver' and the 'shared 25 MiB inline-media cap' cannot be verified from this diff. I have no evidence of a regression, so I am not raising a finding.

T-041 (prefix cache) and the other relevant definitions are unaffected by the changed lines. The unchanged prefix-cache text (cache scope partitioning, bank sizing) is pre-existing.

Open question for integration: whether the code change behind this doc raises the cap consistently with the ingress reservation (charge covering a 40 MiB body plus base64 decode copies), and whether the new `media_too_large` error path avoids leaking plaintext content or bypassing the memory reservation. That code is not in this batch, so it needs review in whichever unit contains it.
